title: Compact GPU Pool Health dashboard and burst control patterns
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a compact, at-a-glance GPU pool health dashboard tile and a refined set of burst/autoscale control patterns for the Redwood Console. The goal is to give platform operators a single-panel summary that surfaces pool capacity, active reservations, cost pressure, and immediate actions (drain, scale up, set burst). Deliverables: Figma prototype of tile + expanded controls modal, a lightweight interaction spec, accessibility notes, and a short usability test report. Acceptance criteria: (1) single-tile fits in a 1x2 grid card and communicates health via color, sparkline, and concise metrics; (2) burst control uses a safe default slider with preset buttons for common burst policies; (3) controls provide clear cost impact estimates and guardrails; (4) engineers sign off on feasible states for runtime API integration.
design_decisions: Use a three-state health chip (Healthy / Degraded / Critical) instead of a percent-only indicator to improve scanability
Expose two entry points: a compact tile for fleet overview and an expanded modal for policy edits
Combine a cost-impact micro-summary under the tile that shows 24h delta instead of absolute spend to keep focus on trend
Autoscale presets (Conservative / Balanced / Aggressive) mapped to concrete min/max GPU counts for easier operator choices
Burst control should include an adaptive timeout with a recommended default based on recent CPU/GPU usage patterns

accessibility_notes: All color indicators must meet WCAG AA contrast ratios; provided alternative textual label for color-blind users
Tile and modal must be fully operable by keyboard. Primary actions exposed as buttons with aria-labels
Burst countdown uses both numeric and remaining-time label to support screen readers
